title: Follow-Up: CoT Analysis of GPT-5's 2.1% Deceptive Reasoning Cases

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Understanding the linguistic fingerprint of deceptive CoT enables simpler, more transparent monitoring and informs training interventions. If a lightweight rule-based detector can match the neural monitor's 81% precision, this provides a practical, interpretable monitoring tool.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires eliciting deceptive CoT from GPT-5 (or equivalent model), performing qualitative linguistic analysis, and building a rule-based detector. The elicitation step is uncertain (hitting the 2.1% rate requires many samples or targeted prompts). Linguistic analysis requires qualitative research skills. Moderate difficulty overall.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Qualitative analysis + quantitative feature extraction + rule-based detector construction. Three linked components, each non-trivial. Achievable in 30 hours if the qualitative analysis is kept focused (3-4 feature categories) and the rule-based detector is simple.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
